key_insight: Continuous generative flows and diffusion models can be applied to language modelling by operating directly in token embedding space, enabling effective continuous-language generation with only minimal changes to discrete-token pipelines.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between powerful continuous generative models (diffusion/flow) and discrete-language data, avoiding heavy discrete-only adaptations while retaining token-level semantics.
method: Map discrete tokens into a continuous embedding space (use pretrained token embeddings or a lightweight encoder).
Train a continuous flow/diffusion model on embedded representations to model latent trajectories and noise processes.
Decode modeled embeddings back to tokens with a simple decoder (e.g., softmax over vocabulary or nearest-neighbor in embedding space), keeping architecture changes minimal.
impact: Makes continuous generative techniques (flows/diffusion) practical for language tasks, offering smoother latent control, improved integration with multimodal continuous data, and an easy retrofit path for existing token-based models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Tokenizer → Embeddings → Flow/Diffusion model → Decoder → Tokens
Embedding-space visualization: trajectories showing how flows/diffusion transform embeddings over time
Comparison chart: discrete-token DLM vs. embedding-space ELF highlighting adaptation complexity and advantages
Icon set: pretrained embeddings, continuous flow, lightweight decoder, minimal-change badge
paper_authors: Keya Hu, Linlu Qiu, Yiyang Lu, Hanhong Zhao, Tianhong Li
